:::{#lem-mahalanobis-nonneg}
#### The quadratic form in the multivariate normal density is non-negative

If $\matr{\covmat}$ is a $p \times p$ positive definite matrix
and $\vx, \vecf{\mean} \in \reals^p$, then

$$\tp{(\vx - \vecf{\mean})} \matr{\covmat}^{-1} (\vx - \vecf{\mean}) \ge 0,$$

with equality if and only if $\vx = \vecf{\mean}$.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{\covmat}^{-1}$ is positive definite
([positive definite inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#thm-pd-inverse)).
If $\vx \neq \vecf{\mean}$, then $\vx - \vecf{\mean} \neq \vzero$,
so the quadratic form is positive by the
[definition of positive definite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite).
If $\vx = \vecf{\mean}$, then $\vx - \vecf{\mean} = \vzero$,
and the quadratic form is $0$.

:::
